headline: Tk 24 crore gold seized: 12kg gold paste found in underwear at Dhaka airport
summary: Customs officials discovered the gold hidden in the clothing of two passengers arriving from Dubai on Emirates flight EK586.
details: Dhaka Customs House seized 12.06 kg of gold paste with an estimated market value of approximately Tk 24 crore.
The gold was discovered hidden inside the jeans and underwear of two passengers, Chen Liyun and Mo Xiaoyou, who had arrived from Dubai on Emirates flight EK586.
Customs authorities acted on a secret tip-off and began monitoring passengers at the baggage belt-2 area after they completed immigration.
Initial tests confirmed that the recovered gold is 24-carat purity.
Legal proceedings under the Customs Act 2023 and the Penal Code are currently underway against the two detained passengers and the seized gold.
caption:

Customs authorities acted on a secret tip-off and began monitoring passengers at the baggage belt-2 area after they completed immigration.

Initial tests confirmed that the recovered gold is 24-carat purity.

Legal proceedings under the Customs Act 2023 and the Penal Code are currently underway against the two detained passengers and the seized gold.

headline: DMCH ambulance strike: Private ambulance owners suspend strike for 7 days
summary: Patients and their families faced severe hardships as private ambulance drivers struck over parking space demands; the strike has now been paused for a week.
details: Private ambulance owners and drivers at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) have suspended their strike for seven days.
The strike was launched to demand permanent parking spaces for ambulances at the hospital area.
During the strike, patients and their families faced extreme hardship, struggling to find transport for emergency care or to take deceased bodies home.
Many were forced to use alternative vehicles to transport patients from the hospital, causing significant distress and delays.
The suspension of the strike provides temporary relief to thousands of patients who rely on DMCH services daily.
caption:
Patients stranded and families in distress as ambulance drivers strike over parking spaces.

Private ambulance owners and drivers at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) have suspended their strike for seven days.

The strike was launched to demand permanent parking spaces for ambulances at the hospital area.

During the strike, patients and their families faced extreme hardship, struggling to find transport for emergency care or to take deceased bodies home.

Many were forced to use alternative vehicles to transport patients from the hospital, causing significant distress and delays.

The suspension of the strike provides temporary relief to thousands of patients who rely on DMCH services daily.
